editorial:
Imagine being nineteen years old and deciding to fly across the country to find a father who hasn't been in your life for sixteen years. That is exactly what Libby does in this sweet, quirky story. You get to follow her from New York to the sunny streets of Los Angeles, where she is determined to get some answers. The movie has a light, breezy feel to it, focusing on the awkward and funny moments that happen when a daughter meets a dad who is a bit of a Hollywood flake. It is less about big drama and more about the small, human connections that form when people are forced to be honest with each other.

You will really love the chemistry between the characters, especially how Libby handles her dad's chaotic lifestyle. The pacing is steady, though it feels more like a play than a big blockbuster. If you enjoy character-driven stories with a lot of heart, this is right up your alley. Since it is an older gem, you might want to look for it to rent on Apple TV or see if it is streaming on Prime Video. If you are a movie collector, adding the Blu-ray to your physical collection is a great way to keep this cozy story forever.
endingExplained: After spending time with her father and meeting the colorful people in his life, Libby realizes that her dad is flawed but genuinely cares for her. Instead of a huge fight or a dramatic breakup, they find a way to accept each other for who they are. The movie ends on a hopeful note, showing that while their relationship isn't perfect, they have finally started a real bond that can actually last.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cozy family dramas and stories about reconciliation.
